title: Morning kernel tinker log - Samir
content:
(quick morning scratchpad)

Summary:
- Woke up to a 11:30am alert: p99 token latency spike on americana-prod (host-pool-3). Spike correlates with a small subset of requests (~0.9% of traffic) hitting a specific seq_len pattern (prefix ~512 + burst tokens).
- Goal today: reproduce locally, identify where KV cache pressure / mutex contention happens, and sketch a mitigation that doesn't require immediate infra churn.

Observations / immediate hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: KV cache eviction thrashing when request uses long prefix then streams. Eviction + re-materialize costs hit p99.
- Hypothesis B: Serialization lock (cache/kv map) sees rare O(n) path for unusual sequence lengths -> single-thread stall.
- Hypothesis C: GPU kernel fallback for 2nd chunk due to padding/sequence alignment causing a synchronizing operation.

Repro steps (local) tried so far:
1) checkout: git checkout -b samir/p99-investigate && git pull origin main
2) dataset: small-repro.json (created minimal input. see below)
3) run: ./dev/run_infer.sh --model Llama-3 --seq-prefix 512 --burst 64 --repeat 1000 --profile
4) perf capture: sudo perf record -F 99 -g -p <pid> -- sleep 10 then perf report

Quick results: (ran 3 iter)
- One run shows 3x syscalls in allocator path when prefix ~512.
- perf report shows 'kv_cache::evict' and 'mutex::lock_slowpath' as callers at p99 stack.
- CUDA traces: occasional cudaDeviceSynchronize around chunk boundary (suspect alignment).

Commands I used (for reference):
- python tools/create_repro_input.py --prefix 512 --burst 64 -o small-repro.json
- ./dev/local_infer --config conf/local.yaml --input small-repro.json --trace=tokprof.log
- sudo perf record -F 99 -g -p $(pgrep local_infer) -- sleep 15
- perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded; flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg

Notes in code to inspect: 
- serving/runtime/kv_cache.cpp: look at evict() path; there is a TODO about coarse-grain lock in commit 1c9e2f7.
- serving/runtime/request_router.cpp: check batch boundary logic around chunking/aligner.
- cuda/kernels/aligner.cu: see comments about fallback for non-power-of-two seq_len.

Small triage TODOs (priority ordering):
- [ ] Add lightweight tracing around kv_cache evict path (emit small event with prefix_len + current_size) - low risk. (samir) DUE: EOD
- [ ] Run repro on dedicated dev-gpu-2 with NVPROF to check kernel launch times (nadia/help) - request slot 2pm
- [ ] Add temporary per-request metric: cache_hits_before_infer, cache_evictions_during_infer - short-term telemetry (omar)
- [ ] Try replica run with disabled eviction (config flag) to see if p99 disappears (safe toggle) - if yes, consider temporary rollout to reduce visible errors.
- [ ] Open PR for a guarded fast-path using try_lock in evict() to avoid long stall (sketch below).

Sketch for guarded try_lock fast path (pseudocode):
- bool tryEvictFast() {
-   if (!evict_mutex.try_lock()) return false;
-   ... perform small bounded eviction ...
-   evict_mutex.unlock();
-   return true;
- }
- On hot path: if (!tryEvictFast()) enqueue eviction task to background queue and continue with best-effort KV read.

Risks: returning best-effort KV read may serve stale KV and could degrade output quality. Need gating and observability (A/B test to 0.5% traffic).

Telemetry notes (short):
- current metrics exist: kv_cache.size, kv_cache.evictions.total, kv_cache.hits.total but not per-request or per-prefix. Need cardinality guards.
- Create metric: tag with prefix_bucket (256/512/1024) and stream to flame-kv channel for 72h.

Meeting notes / folks to sync:
- Sync with Nadia 2:10pm: share perf and nvprof.
- Quick async to Omar: ask to add temporary metric and a toggle flag.
- If guarded try_lock reduces p99 locally -> coordinate with SRE for small canary (1% traffic) and in-flight roll back plan.

Random mental notes (for later):
- Might be worth exploring a compact LRU for prefixes vs whole request (cache_key = hash(prefix_bytes) to reduce memory churn).
- Check client-side SDK: some callers may send excessive metadata causing larger serialized requests; look for pattern from mobile app 5.3.2.

Open questions: 
- Would background eviction and best-effort read tighten latency enough or will it push cost elsewhere (more allocations)?
- Are there any similar incidents in the last 6 months? quick search in alerts shows one in 2024-10 but was attributed to infra patch (need deeper compare).

Local artifacts:
- small-repro.json (in /tmp/repro/samir/), tokprof.log, perf.data (compressed: perf-samir-20250212.tar.gz)

Next steps (my plan for the afternoon):
- morning: add tracing and minimal try_lock sketch in branch (1h)
- lunch: repro on dev-gpu-2 + nvprof (45m)
- 2pm: sync w/ Nadia (30m)
- post-sync: iterate on guarded path and push small PR for review (aim to get CI green and perf test in sandbox)

Notes-to-self: keep PR tiny. Add feature flag. Add metrics. No infra changes before we know it's safe.

---
Choppy TODO list (for copying into ticket):
- repro + perf capture (done)
- add per-request eviction tracing (in progress)
- nvprof run (pending)
- sketch try_lock fast path + metrics (in progress)
- create Linear ticket with rollback plan and canary plan (samir)
